summary: The note describes the "Every Step Counts" campaign, launched September 5, 2023, which weaves physical fitness into daily community life through public spaces, walkability projects, schools, workplaces, seniors' programs, a fitness app and festivals. It profiles related initiatives and the local figures involved. It closes by noting accessibility and inclusion challenges, which are being addressed with sliding-scale pricing, grants and scholarships.
one_line: A local "Every Step Counts" campaign launched in 2023 integrates fitness into community life via parks, walkable infrastructure, schools, workplaces, seniors' programs, an app and festivals.
key_facts: The "Every Step Counts" campaign launched on September 5, 2023, and was created by Dr. Samantha Rodriguez, a prominent public health advocate.
"Every Step Counts" is led by the local Public Health Department and community organizations, and aims to integrate exercise into community routines rather than just advocate it.

Since October 2023, municipal parks with new fitness stations host free weekly fitness classes, including yoga and high-intensity interval training, led by instructors such as certified personal trainer Mark Thompson.
The "Connected Communities" project launched in November 2023 to build and revitalize pedestrian pathways, crosswalks and cycling lanes.
Jane Parker, the city's Chief Infrastructure Officer, reported a 30% increase in daily foot traffic since the Connected Communities project started.
The "Active Students, Active Futures" initiative put daily physical activity into school curriculums starting in late September 2023 and encourages inter-school sports tournaments.
Kyle Richards, Assistant Principal of Oakwood Elementary School, says students are more focused in class and excited about school-organized sports.
Emily Harris of TechForge Inc. says employee productivity and morale improved since "Fitness Fridays" began on September 12, 2023.
The "Golden Age Fitness" program, launched in October 2023, offers seniors low-impact aerobic classes, water aerobics and walking clubs; veteran Joseph Allen leads a walking group.
The free FitCommunity app, launched September 20, 2023, tracks activity and offers fitness challenges, local event information and rewards for meeting goals.
The Annual Health Harvest Fest debuted on October 3, 2023, with fitness demonstrations, healthy food vendors and free health screenings.

To address accessibility and inclusion challenges, efforts include sliding-scale pricing for classes, community grants for low-income families to buy sports equipment, and scholarships for young athletes.
